lines.japanese: 朝。
lines.english: Morning.

lines.japanese: 定刻通りに起床した僕は、部屋の空気を入れ換えがてら、寝ぼけた頭を氷水みたいな風に晒していた。
lines.english: I woke at my usual time and opened the window to air out my room, letting a wind like ice water wash over my half-asleep head.

lines.japanese: そろそろ布団を畳もうかなと立ちあがったとき、ドアが控えめにノックされた。
lines.english: Just as I stood to fold up my futon, someone knocked timidly at the door.

lines.japanese: 「お、お兄ちゃん……朝ごはんできてる……」
lines.english: “B-Big Brother... breakfast is ready...”

lines.japanese: 小鳩が僕を兄と呼んでくれるようになって何週間か経っているけれど、まだ彼女にはいささかの照れがあるみたいで、たとえば一日の始まりなどにはその言葉に愛らしい緊張が含まれていたりする。
lines.english: Several weeks had passed since Kobato began calling me her brother, but the word still seemed to embarrass her a little. At the start of the day, for instance, it could carry an adorably nervous note.

lines.japanese: そんなぎこちなさには気付かないふりをし、僕はドアを開けてすぐ行くよと自然に微笑む。
lines.english: I pretended not to notice her awkwardness, opened the door, and gave her a natural smile as I said I'd be right there.

lines.japanese: 「きのう和食だったから、きょうはパンだよ」
lines.english: “We had Japanese food yesterday, so today we're having bread.”

lines.japanese: そうすれば、徐々に普段の──叔父さんや叔母さんやお友達の吉川さんと接するときのような──元気で明るい小鳩に戻ってくれるんだ。
lines.english: That gradually brought back the usual cheerful, energetic Kobato—the one who appeared around her aunt and uncle, or her friend Yoshikawa.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、あの何も付けなくても美味しいパン？」
lines.english: “Oh, is it that bread that's good even without anything on it?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、そう。花水木通りにできたお店の」
lines.english: “Yeah. From that shop that opened on Flowering Dogwood Street.”

lines.japanese: 「いわゆるパン屋さんのパンだ。うん、あの店はいいよ」
lines.english: “What you might call real bakery bread. Yes, that place is good.”

lines.japanese: 「私が見つけたの」
lines.english: “I found it.”

lines.japanese: 「そうなんだ。お手柄だね、小鳩」
lines.english: “Did you? Good work, Kobato.”

lines.japanese: 「えへへ、まあねー」
lines.english: “Ehehe. I know.”

lines.japanese: 最近はもう、小鳩の笑顔を見るのも珍しいことではなかった。
lines.english: By now, seeing Kobato smile was no longer a rare event.

lines.japanese: 僕が面白い冗談を言えないのは相変わらずだけど、彼女は親愛のしるしとして温かい表情を作ってくれる。
lines.english: I was as incapable as ever of telling an amusing joke, but she gave me warm expressions as signs of affection.

lines.japanese: 僕は知った。一日の最初と終わりに笑顔を交換する関係。たぶん、これが家族なんだろう。
lines.english: I had learned what it was to exchange smiles at the beginning and end of each day. This, perhaps, was what it meant to be a family.

lines.japanese: 家族の食卓。
lines.english: The family breakfast table.

lines.japanese: 僕らは兄妹ふたり、朝食をとりながら朝の情報番組を観賞していた。
lines.english: The two of us, brother and sister, watched the morning news program as we ate.

lines.japanese: 「あ、御影クリヤ。これ売れてるよね、いい曲だよね」
lines.english: “Oh, Kuriya Mikage. This song's selling really well, isn't it? It's good.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ……どれ？　どの曲？」
lines.english: “Huh...? Which one? Which song?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、消えちゃったか。いや、いま流れてた曲」
lines.english: “Oh, it's gone. The song that was just playing.”

lines.japanese: 「あや……ごめん、聞いてなかった」
lines.english: “Oh... Sorry, I wasn't listening.”

lines.japanese: 「ええー？　いい曲だったのに」
lines.english: “What? But it was such a good song.”

lines.japanese: 「でも私、クリヤあんまり好きじゃない」
lines.english: “I don't really like KuRiYa.”

lines.japanese: 「知ってるけど、いまの曲は小鳩でも好きそうだったよ」
lines.english: “I know, but I thought even you might like that song.”

lines.japanese: 「ふーん、じゃあこんど聞いてみる」
lines.english: “Hmm. Then I'll listen to it sometime.”

lines.japanese: 「そうそう、食わず嫌いは良くないよ。世界を狭めるからね」
lines.english: “Exactly. You shouldn't decide you dislike something before you try it. That makes your world smaller.”

lines.japanese: 「お兄ちゃんは何でもかんでも聞きすぎだよ。もっとしゅたいせーを持たなきゃ」
lines.english: “You listen to anything and everything, Big Brother. You need a mind of your own.”

lines.japanese: 「はは、言われちゃった」
lines.english: “Haha. You got me.”

lines.japanese: 「えへ、言ってやったー」
lines.english: “Ehe. I sure did.”

lines.japanese: かつての僕らは互いに遠慮しすぎていた。
lines.english: Once, we had both been far too reserved around each other.

lines.japanese: 無口なふたりのあいだに下りる沈黙を、探り探りな言葉で晴らしてゆくことに精一杯だった。
lines.english: We had devoted all our effort to cautiously searching for words that might dispel the silence descending between two quiet people.

lines.japanese: いまでも会話の内容はほとんど変わらない。花も実もない無為なやり取りだ。
lines.english: Even now, the substance of our conversations had hardly changed. They were idle exchanges with neither flower nor fruit.

lines.japanese: けれど、あの強迫観念のように口を開かされていた空々しい兄妹ごっことは、もう違う。
lines.english: But this was no longer that hollow game of brother and sister, when something like an obsession had compelled us to keep opening our mouths.

lines.japanese: 他愛もないものを他愛もないまま口にする。思ったことを思ったまま伝える。そうして肩肘張らないことによって余裕が生まれる。余裕があれば笑顔もこぼれる。
lines.english: We said trivial things and let them remain trivial. We shared a thought exactly as it came. Once we stopped straining so hard, we found room to breathe. And with that room came smiles.

lines.japanese: 気付いてしまえば簡単なことだったんだ。
lines.english: It had been simple once we noticed it.

lines.japanese: 『まあ、見てくださいこの指輪。素敵ですねー、こんな指輪プレゼントされちゃったら、女性はみんなクラッときちゃいますよねー』
lines.english: “My, look at this ring. Isn't it lovely? Any woman would go weak in the knees if someone gave her a ring like this.”

lines.japanese: 「このひと、いつもおんなじこと言ってる」
lines.english: “That lady always says the same thing.”

lines.japanese: 「そう？　台本なのかな」
lines.english: “Does she? Maybe it's in the script.”

lines.japanese: 「しゅたいせーがないのかも」
lines.english: “Maybe she doesn’t have a mind of her own.”

lines.japanese: 「そうだね」
lines.english: “You may be right.”

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “Yeah.”

lines.japanese: ふたり、しばらくテレビに見入る。
lines.english: For a while, the two of us watched the television in silence.

lines.japanese: ちょっと前までの僕は、どうして無言の空白をあんなにも恐れていたのだろう。
lines.english: Why had I been so afraid of those wordless gaps until just recently?

lines.japanese: 会話なんかなくても安らげる、それが我が家という空間なのに。
lines.english: Home was the one place where we could be at peace without any conversation at all.

lines.japanese: 僕たちは食事を進めながら、しばし心地の良い沈黙を愉しんでいた。
lines.english: As we continued our breakfast, we spent a while enjoying the comfortable silence.

lines.japanese: 話すのは話したいときだけでいいんだ。
lines.english: We only had to speak when we wanted to.

lines.japanese: 『えー、近ごろ若い女性のあいだで、スープスタンドやお茶漬けバーといった軽い食事をとれる店が注目されています』
lines.english: “Lately, shops where customers can enjoy a light meal—soup stands and ochazuke bars, for example—have begun attracting attention among young women.”

lines.japanese: 「お茶漬け？」
lines.english: “Ochazuke?”

lines.japanese: 話したいときが訪れた。
lines.english: The desire to speak had arrived.

lines.japanese: 「小鳩、お茶漬け好きだよね。見て、注目されてるって。流行先取りだよ、やったね」
lines.english: “You love ochazuke, don't you, Kobato? Look, they say it's getting attention. You were ahead of the trend. Good for you.”

lines.japanese: 「わ、ほんとだ。私すごい、時代にびんかん」
lines.english: “Wow, you’re right. I’m amazing. So in touch with the times.”

lines.japanese: パリのリストランテみたいな洒落た内装が映しだされて、ドレッシーな調理服のスタッフが、黒塗りの膳を運んでくる。
lines.english: The screen showed a fashionable interior like a Parisian ristorante, where a server in dressy chef's whites carried out a black lacquer tray.

lines.japanese: 羽田家の食卓に出る、冷や飯にお茶をかける料理とはまるで別物みたいだ。
lines.english: It looked nothing like the dish made by pouring tea over cold rice that appeared on the Haneda family table.

lines.japanese: 「あれ？　なんかちがう。あのおちゃづけ、まちがってる」
lines.english: “Huh? Something's wrong. That ochazuke is wrong.”

lines.japanese: 「うーん、まだ時代は小鳩に追いついてないのかも」
lines.english: “Hmm. Maybe the times haven't caught up with you yet.”

lines.japanese: 「さいせんたんの女です」
lines.english: “I'm a state-of-the-art woman.”

lines.japanese: 画面の向こうでは、レポーターが上等な陶器を口に付けてさらさらさらと頂いていた。ごく控えめな水音が、かえって視聴者の食欲をそそる。
lines.english: On the other side of the screen, the reporter lifted the fine ceramic bowl to her lips and delicately slurped. The faint sound of water only sharpened the viewers' appetites.

lines.japanese: 「あしたの朝は、うちもおちゃづけにしよっか」
lines.english: “Should we have ochazuke tomorrow morning too?”

lines.japanese: 「それもいいね。小鳩に任せるよ」
lines.english: “That sounds good. I'll leave it to you.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、でもお兄ちゃん、おかゆの方が好きだったよね。じゃあ──」
lines.english: “Oh, but you liked rice porridge better, didn't you, Big Brother? Then—”
“Oh.”

lines.japanese: そう。彼女の想い出の中で粥料理を喜んでいる『お兄ちゃん』は僕じゃない。小鳩はすぐに気付いたみたいだ。
lines.english: Yes. The ‘Big Brother’ who delighted in rice porridge in her memories wasn't me. Kobato seemed to realize it at once.

lines.japanese: 「ごめ、ごめんなさい……」
lines.english: “S-Sorry...”

lines.japanese: 「あはは、いいよ」
lines.english: “Ahaha. It's all right.”

lines.japanese: 不謹慎だから口にはしないけど、僕はそんなうっかり間違いが嬉しかった。
lines.english: It would have been irreverent to say aloud, but that careless mistake made me happy.

lines.japanese: 彼女の中でいつまでも霞むことなく存在しつづける兄の像に、僕も少しは近づけているってことだから。
lines.english: It meant I had drawn at least a little closer to the image of her brother that would live on within her forever, never fading into mist.

lines.japanese: 「謝ることなんかないよ。あんまり深く考えなくていいんだ」
lines.english: “There's nothing to apologize for. You don't need to think so deeply about it.”

lines.japanese: 小鳩が幼い日のヨージ君を忘れるはずはない。そして僕もその清らかな聖域を侵すつもりはない。
lines.english: Kobato would never forget the young Youji. And I had no intention of trespassing upon that sacred place.

lines.japanese: だったら、せめて、彼の現在が僕であると思ってもらいたい。
lines.english: But if nothing else, I wanted her to think of me as the person he was now.

lines.japanese: 「ヨージ君……羽田ヨージは、僕に替わったんじゃない。僕になったんだ」
lines.english: “Youji... Youji Haneda wasn't replaced by me. He became me.”

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 僕は半分嘘をついた。千歳君や成田君が一緒になった今もなお、ヨージ君は奈落の底で膝を抱えているはず。
lines.english: It was half a lie. Even now that Chitose and Narita had joined with me, Youji was surely still crouched at the bottom of the abyss with his arms around his knees.

lines.japanese: けれど彼が妹のためにと生みだした、彼の理想の勇者である僕こそが、彼の望んだ未来であったと──
lines.english: But I was the ideal hero he had created for his sister. I was the future he had wanted—

lines.japanese: ──きっと彼は僕のような大人になっていたはずだと、そう思えるのは本当だから。
lines.english: —and it was true that I believed he would surely have grown into an adult like me.

lines.japanese: 「僕はそのつもりだよ」
lines.english: “That's how I think of it.”

lines.japanese: そして彼もいつか魂の牢獄から羽ばたいて、僕らと一緒になってくれるんだって、心からそう願って。
lines.english: And with all my heart, I hoped that one day he too would soar free of his soul's prison and join us.

lines.japanese: 「小鳩が望むなら、べつにこの先、羽田ヨージを名乗ったっていいし」
lines.english: “If that's what you wanted, I could even call myself Youji Haneda from now on.”

lines.japanese: 勝手にそんなことを決めたら、いろんなひとに迷惑をかけてしまうかもしれないけれど。
lines.english: Arbitrarily deciding such a thing might cause trouble for all sorts of people.

lines.japanese: けれど僕は小鳩の笑顔を守りたいんだ。
lines.english: But I wanted to protect Kobato's smile.

lines.japanese: 与えられた義務だとか果たすべき使命だとか、そんな誰かからのお仕着せじゃなくて、ただ僕が僕の意思で彼女を守りたいんだ。
lines.english: Not because of some duty I'd been given or mission I was obliged to fulfill, nothing imposed on me by somebody else. I simply wanted, of my own free will, to protect her.

lines.japanese: 愛しい妹が笑っていてくれるなら、名前なんかは些細な問題だ。
lines.english: If my beloved little sister could keep smiling, a name was a trivial matter.

lines.japanese: 「……それはいい」
lines.english: “...I don't want that.”

lines.japanese: だけど彼女は首を横に振った。
lines.english: But she shook her head.

lines.japanese: 歳のわりに苦労を重ねてきた小鳩は、こういうことに関して察しのいい子だから、僕の嘘なんか簡単に見破ってしまったのかもしれない。
lines.english: Kobato had endured too much hardship for her age and was perceptive about things like this. Perhaps she had seen through my lie with ease.

lines.japanese: 「タカシお兄ちゃんは、タカシお兄ちゃんだから」
lines.english: “You’re Takashi, my big brother. You’re you.”

lines.japanese: 真面目くさった顔でそう言う彼女は、どんな思いを抱いていたのだろう。
lines.english: What feelings lay behind those words, delivered with such a solemn face?

lines.japanese: 翻せばその言葉は、兄の代わりなんてさせないという拒絶にも取れる。
lines.english: Looked at another way, they could be taken as a refusal to let me act as a substitute for her brother.

lines.japanese: だけど僕の笑顔が崩れてしまうより先に、はにかみながら小鳩が付けたしてくれた。
lines.english: But before my smile could collapse, Kobato shyly added something more.

lines.japanese: 「でも、ありがとう」
lines.english: “But thank you.”

lines.japanese: 「タカシお兄ちゃんも、大事なお兄ちゃん……なんて、えへっ」
lines.english: “You're one of my precious big brothers too, Takashi... Ehehe.”

lines.japanese: 耳まで真っ赤にして俯いてしまった妹を、僕は抱きしめたいと思った。
lines.english: She bowed her head, red all the way to her ears, and I wanted to hug my little sister.

lines.japanese: 年ごろの女の子だから遠慮したけれどね。
lines.english: But she was a girl at a sensitive age, so I restrained myself.

lines.japanese: 祈るまでもなく、世界は今日も平和なんだ。
lines.english: Without any need to pray for it, the world was at peace again today.
